inputs.lease_treatment: B: full lease cash (principal A$70.884m + interest A$15.087m = A$85.971m, 4.47% of revenue) charged in the flows as lease_cost_pct; lease liabilities (A$228.970m) EXCLUDED from net debt; tax EBIT uses D&A ex right-of-use (A$101.137m - A$65.901m = A$35.236m)
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2026 owner FCF = reported FCF 123.080 - lease principal 70.884 - SBC 0.712 - interest income 0 (lease interest is already inside OCF). Embeds a A$21.0m income-tax REFUND and a working-capital release (cash conversion 109%); the forward build starts from components, not from this number.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payment expense' A$0.712m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp); no net-share-settlement tax line disclosed; effectively an SBC-zero market
inputs.interest_income_note: Other income A$0.137m (note 5); net-debt company, nothing to strip
inputs.buyback_note: A$0.921m purchase of treasury shares to satisfy rights (not a capital return); no buyback programme; DRP suspended; no FY26 dividend
inputs.share_count_basis: 672,753,078 ordinary shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 AR note 21) after the Feb-2026 1-for-1.36 entitlement offer issued 333,340,578 shares at A$0.60. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count); unvested performance rights are immaterial (<0.5%). NOT the 441.6m weighted average used for FY26 EPS.
inputs.fy0_nopat_calibration: Modelled FY26: underlying EBITDA 152.5 - lease cash 86.0 - SBC 0.7 - D&A ex-ROU 35.2 = EBIT 30.6; less bank interest ~20.6 = pre-tax ~10 vs reported underlying NPAT 10.8 (tax ~nil). Ties within non-operating noise, so lease and NCI are each charged once.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD, the currency of the flows: AU 10-yr government ~4.4% risk-free + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.3 (small-cap, leveraged, mid-turnaround cyclical) = ~11.6% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt 5.25% (variable-rate facility, FY26 AR note 18) = 3.7% after 30% tax; weights ~73% equity (A$545m market cap) / 27% debt (A$205m) = 9.5%. Applied to ALL three scenarios: turnaround, covenant and control-failure risk is charged once, in the bear-case flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.notes: Owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + section 7). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Base is a MID-CYCLE build: FY26 underlying EBITDA (A$152.5m post-AASB16, A$66.5m pre-AASB16, 3.5% margin) is a trough after mispricing, inventory and control failures; the pre-distress FY19-22 pre-AASB16 margin of 11-13% is a peak the new management has not claimed it can regain. Base recovers to the restated FY25 level (~7.9% pre-AASB16) over 8 years, bull to ~10% (FY23), bear to ~5%. Statutory FY26 EBITDA/NPAT (impairment A$450.4m, of which only A$3.6m cash) is not used. Per-share history is broken by the Feb-2026 raise: all per-share outputs are on 672.75m shares. Working capital sign negative (distributor). Terminal cap 12x owner FCF for a cyclical distributor with a broken track record. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position null.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case mid-path revenue growth (car-parc growth ~2-3% plus modest share recovery), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (-20.5% 3yr, -11.5% 5yr) are driven by A$464m of FY24+FY26 impairments and a A$200m raise at A$0.60, not by the operating business; EPS CAGRs undefined (FY26 EPS -0.977). Owner-FCF CAGRs are working-capital noise (FY21 owner FCF A$16.9m, FY23 A$106.1m, FY26 A$51.5m incl. a A$21m tax refund). Revenue is the only usable series: +1.8% 5yr, -1.6% 3yr. None of them is a forward anchor; the base path is a judgment on margin recovery.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - lease principal - SBC (FY20+; pre-IFRS16 years need no lease deduction). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR -21.4% vs reported -10.6%: the gap is lease principal growing (61->71m) while cash flow shrank, not SBC (immaterial).

bear.ebitda_margin_basis: underlying EBITDA post-AASB16 (company definition, before significant items); lease_cost_pct is charged separately so the pre-AASB16 margin is ebitda_margin - lease_cost_pct
bear.narrative: Bear: the turnaround stalls. Pricing reset and stock availability stabilise Trade but Repco/NAPA and Supercheap keep the share they took in FY25-26; NZ stays in decline; Retail franchise network keeps shrinking. Payroll-underpayment remediation and further control fixes absorb the cost-out. Revenue flat in FY27 then ~1.5%/yr (below car-parc growth). Underlying EBITDA margin (post-AASB16) grinds from 7.9% to only 9.5% -- about 5% after the ~4.45% lease bill, never recovering the restated FY25 level of 7.9% pre-AASB16. The business survives (net leverage stays inside covenants on this path) but equity is worth little: year-10 owner FCF ~A$40m against ~A$140m of net debt and NCI.

base.ebitda_margin_basis: underlying EBITDA post-AASB16 (company definition, before significant items); lease_cost_pct is charged separately so the pre-AASB16 margin is ebitda_margin - lease_cost_pct
base.narrative: Base: FY27 'modest' revenue growth (1.5%) as guided, with Trade parts and Networks growing and Retail/NZ/equipment still soft; from FY28 revenue tracks car-parc growth plus some share recovery (3-3.5%), fading to 2.5%. Underlying EBITDA margin (post-AASB16) rebuilds from 7.9% (FY26) to ~12.3% by FY34 -- ~7.85% after the lease bill, i.e. back to the restated FY25 pre-AASB16 level (7.9%) and well below the FY19-22 peak of 11-13%. Management says FY27 benefits are reinvested in technology and people, so year-1 margin gain is small. Cash tax shielded at 15%/25% in FY27-28 by FY25-26 tax losses, then 30% statutory. Capex held at ~D&A ex-ROU (1.8%), above the FY27 guide of 'in line with FY26' (1.5%). Working capital consumes 15c per dollar of revenue growth (distributor: inventory + receivables exceed payables).

bull.ebitda_margin_basis: underlying EBITDA post-AASB16 (company definition, before significant items); lease_cost_pct is charged separately so the pre-AASB16 margin is ebitda_margin - lease_cost_pct
bull.narrative: Bull: the Wilesmith turnaround executes like Supercheap's playbook -- pricing/ranging discipline restores Trade gross margin, the strategy reset divests sub-scale non-core assets, cost-out lands, and store network growth resumes; independent-workshop share gains and the ageing car parc lift revenue 4-5%/yr in FY28-31. Underlying EBITDA margin (post-AASB16) recovers to 14.5% -- ~10% pre-AASB16, roughly the FY23 level (9.4%) and still short of the FY19-22 peak. A private-equity or trade approach (Bain at A$5.40 in 2024 on the old 339m share count, Jefferies flagging renewed interest post-result) is the realisation path but is not modelled as a separate exit multiple.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting interim owner FCF and exiting in year 10 earns a 15% IRR; terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, 12x FCF10)), net debt + NCI deducted, per share on the flat 672.75m count. Probability-weighted across scenarios.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at its own rate (min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF10)). 15% row equals the base entry price; 9.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; each cell rebuilds TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 12x FCF10)). The 12x cap binds across most of the grid, which is why the g-axis is flat: the valuation is a multiple-on-recovered-FCF call, not a perpetuity-growth call.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (house default 15%): three years of guidance cuts, restatements, a payroll-underpayment review still open, covenant relief that reverts through FY27, and a turnaround whose first non-downgrade update came only in Aug-2026 -- the bear case is a live path, not a tail. Bull cut to 20% (default 35%) because it needs margin recovery, a clean strategy reset AND no further control surprises to land together; the M&A floor is speculation, not an approach. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is A$0.7m (0.04% of revenue): house and street values differ by ~A$0.02/share, so the accounting-regime band collapses to a point relative to the price; band_position is null rather than a degenerate or off-scale number.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A distressed-turnaround distributor valued on the cash it can earn once margins normalise, not on the trough (FY26) or the peak (FY19-22). The 12x terminal cap means value is a multiple of recovered owner FCF; each 1pp of terminal pre-AASB16 EBITDA margin is worth roughly A$0.20/share in the base case.
key_judgments: Mid-cycle pre-AASB16 EBITDA margin: base 7.85% (=restated FY25), bull 10%, bear 5%
Lease treatment B, so net debt is bank debt only (A$137.8m) and the 4.45% lease bill is a permanent operating cost
Flat 672.75m share count: SBC expensed, no further dilution assumed -- another raise would be a bear-case event beyond what is modelled
Risk charged in flows and weights (30% bear), single 9.5% AUD WACC across scenarios
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_it: 1H27 result (Feb-2027): Trade gross-margin trajectory, whether NLR stays under 3.0x at the Dec-2026 test, strategy-reset divestments and any further restatement. A confirmed takeover approach would replace this frame with deal-completes/deal-breaks weighting.

warnings: Per-share history is broken at FY2026 by the 1-for-1.36 raise (339.4m -> 672.75m shares); never compare pre-FY26 EPS/DPS with these outputs.
FY26 owner FCF of A$51.5m includes a A$21.0m tax refund and a working-capital release; the underlying run-rate before WC and tax was ~A$36m.
Bear case does not model a second equity raise or covenant breach; if the Dec-2026 NLR test fails, equity value falls below the bear figure.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
